headline: Verdict today in crimes against humanity case against Obaidul Quader & 6 others for July uprising atrocities
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its judgment today after an eight-month trial. The case involves allegations of widespread atrocities during the 2024 July uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 is set to deliver its verdict today in a crimes against humanity case. The case involves Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and six others, accused of atrocities during the July uprising in 2024.

After approximately eight months of trial, the tribunal announced yesterday that the verdict would be delivered today. All seven accused, including Quader, former state minister Mohammad Ali Arafat, and AL Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim, are currently absconding.

Other prominent figures accused include Jubo League Chairman Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash, its General Secretary Moinul Hossain Nikhil, Chhatra League President Saddam Hussain, and its General Secretary Sheikh Wali Asif Enan. Quader, a four-time minister and three-term AL general secretary, is central to the prosecution's allegations.

The prosecution alleges that Quader, in his capacity as AL general secretary and a cabinet minister, exercised command and control over law enforcement agencies and armed cadres. These forces were reportedly used to violently suppress the quota reform movement that began on July 1, 2024.

More than 1,400 protesters were allegedly killed and over 25,000 seriously injured in widespread, systematic, and targeted attacks on the civilian population. These actions were reportedly carried out with the knowledge and involvement of the accused.

Nasim is accused of helping organize the party's response, while Arafat allegedly controlled media and suppressed reports of violence. Parash and Nikhil are accused of mobilizing Jubo League activists, with Nikhil specifically alleged to have opened fire on protesters.

BCL leaders Saddam and Enan are accused of assembling armed cadres and coordinating attacks during the uprising. The investigation began on June 18, 2025, leading to the framing of seven charges on January 22, 2026, and a trial with 29 prosecution witnesses.

headline_marked: [[Jinnah photos in Ducsu archive spark backlash]] at Dhaka University, investigation launched
headline: Jinnah photos in Ducsu archive spark backlash at Dhaka University, investigation launched
summary: Controversy erupted after three photos of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah were displayed in the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) archive, leading to protests and a university investigation.
details: A major controversy has erupted at Dhaka University after three photos of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah were displayed in the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) archive. The move sparked immediate criticism on social media and led to protests from various student groups.
On Monday, an enraged student tore down Jinnah's photos in protest. Nationalist Student Party (Chhatra Dal) and Bangladesh Students' Union also voiced strong opposition to the display.

The Ducsu archive, which houses rare photographs and documents of historical events related to the subcontinent and Bangladesh's independence struggle, reopened recently after renovation. Among the newly added items were Jinnah's photos, including one from his 1948 speech declaring Urdu as the sole state language of Pakistan.

Notably, photos of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, a leader of Bangladesh's independence movement, which were previously present, were reportedly removed or not included in the new display. This further fueled the controversy among students and political organizations.

SM Forhad, General Secretary of Ducsu, defended the inclusion of Jinnah's photos, stating that they were accompanied by captions detailing his anti-Bengali language stance. He argued that omitting them would be seen as an attempt to hide his historical position.

The student who tore the photos, Abu Tayeb Habildar, a student of the Urdu Department, stated that Jinnah, who opposed Bengali as a state language and arrested students in 1948, should not have a place in Ducsu. He had also contested the last Ducsu VP election.

In a separate protest, the Student Federation displayed a photo of former Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes in 1981, placing it above Jinnah's photos. They cited a similar rationale of "doing what they wished."

Following a day of protests and criticism, the Dhaka University administration assured an investigation and formed a committee led by Pro-Vice Chancellor (Administration) Professor Mohammad Almojadded Alfehsani. The committee will also investigate other unauthorized installations on campus.
caption:
